messages:
emma: hitting a weird spike in 502s from the edge region (us-west-2). looks like NAT/egress is the suspect, errors show ECONNRESET when pulling models and spikes in TIME_WAIT.
raj: logs? any convtrack / netstat numbers?
olivia: saw this earlier — model pull fanout after autoscale causes bursts. we may be exhausting ephemeral ports on the NATs.
luis: confirmed from bastion: netstat -an | grep TIME_WAIT | wc -l -> ~54k, conntrack shows high counts too. 502s align with model-puller flaps.
emma: right. errors: "failed to connect: no available ports" in runtime logs. Also registry 429s from ECR at same time.
raj: short term: we can add an extra NAT gateway in the AZ and shift a subset of subnets to it to double the port pool. can also add EIP-backed NAT instances if we need quick control.
olivia: +1. Also we should enable VPC endpoints for ECR and S3 to avoid registry egress for model pulls. that will reduce external port usage a lot.
luis: practical playbook I'm testing: 1) create new NAT GW in us-west-2b, attach new route table, move worker subnets handling model warmups; 2) add a small rate limiter in the model pull controller to stagger pulls (random jitter); 3) create ECR interface endpoint + S3 gateway endpoint; 4) temporary registry pull proxy (single IP) for bursts.
emma: can you paste the iptables/conntrack commands you used?
luis: sure — run on a node:
```
# conntrack summary
sudo conntrack -S | head -n 20
# TIME_WAIT count
ss -s | grep -i time_wait
# list active NAT gw flows from nat gateway metrics
# check aws cloudwatch: NATGatewayActiveConnections and PortUsage
```
raj: metrics to watch: NATGatewayBytesOut, ActiveConnections, PortExhaustion alarms. set alarm when TIME_WAIT > 40k or active connections > 50k per nat.
emma: ops question — will adding NATs require DNS changes for the model-registry domain?
olivia: no, not DNS. route table changes only. but the load will shift per-subnet. also keep in mind ephemeral ports are per NAT EIP; adding NATs spreads the 5-tuple space.
deploy-bot: deploy started: model-puller v2.3 -> staging (staggered pull enabled). ETA 2m.
raj: mid-term improvements we should prioritize: connection pooling at the registry client, keep-alive reuse, and avoiding frequent new TLS handshakes for each model chunk. also rewrite the model bootstrap to fetch manifests first, then parallelize layer pulls with a bounded concurrency of ~50 per node.
emma: long-term: consider an internal artifact cache (per-AZ) + shared prefix cache so we avoid cross-AZ egress. also evaluate using NAT gateways per subfleet vs centralized NAT.
olivia: note for runbooks: when you see >60k TIME_WAIT on nat, treat as port exhaustion risk — apply immediate mitigations (add nat, enable endpoints, throttle pulls). document how to rollback route table changes.
luis: after route change + ECR endpoint + staggered pulls we saw active connections drop by ~70% and 502s disappeared. leaving notes in runbook.
emma: awesome. can someone open a CR with: 1) add ECR/S3 endpoints to default worker VPC template, 2) add staggered pull logic to model-puller, 3) runbook for NAT surge?
raj: opening CR now -> #4567. linking grafana panels and cloudwatch queries.
emma: thanks — tagging oncall for the night: @olivia please keep an eye on nat alarms. :thumbsup:
sre-bot: alert resolved: NAT Port-Exhaustion alarm cleared for us-west-2 at 15:42 UTC.
emma: closing the thread, saved runbook to /runbooks/network/nat-port-exhaustion.md and CR linked.
luis: saved perf charts to the ticket.
